title: Graphic
coreIdea: Reduce the street to pure formal elements — shape, line, contrast, color block, geometry — so the picture works primarily through visual structure.
whyItMatters: Formal strength is the foundation underneath narrative. A picture with strong graphic bones can carry weak content; interesting content with weak form usually fails.
shootingBrief: High-contrast shapes, strong diagonals, color fields, repeating geometry, silhouettes. Minimum 8 frames that succeed primarily on formal terms. Volume 40–70.
technicalFocus: Settings: Careful exposure for contrast. Protect highlights for deep blacks.
Focusing: On the key graphic plane.
Stance: Precise framing and edge control are essential.
Light: Hard light or strong color contrast preferred.
failureModes: Weak formal structure dressed up as graphic.
Busy frames lacking a clear dominant shape or line.

goodVsExcellent.good: Strong shapes or lines are present.
goodVsExcellent.excellent: Formal arrangement is so clear the picture holds power even if the subject is not immediately identifiable.

title: Children
coreIdea: Photograph children in public space with genuine interest in their world, strict dignity, and clear ethical limits.
whyItMatters: Children are a high-stakes subject. Doing this well builds emotional intelligence, timing for unpredictable movement, and personal ethical boundaries for all street portraiture.
shootingBrief: Children playing, walking with adults, or occupying public space. Prefer wider context over tight facial close-ups of strangers' children. Minimum 6 frames. Move on if a parent shows discomfort. Volume 40–60.
technicalFocus: Settings: Fast shutter (often 1/500s+), AF-C with tracking.
Stance: Lower angles frequently work better and feel less predatory.
Distance: Respectful. Wider context is safer and often stronger.
failureModes: Tight faces of strangers' children without context.

goodVsExcellent.good: A decent, non-exploitative picture of a child.
goodVsExcellent.excellent: Shows the child's world with dignity and the same formal strength you would demand of any adult subject.

title: Projects
coreIdea: Work one narrow idea, place, or theme for the entire session so the pictures begin to form a coherent set.
whyItMatters: Isolated exercises produce isolated pictures. Projects create coherence, deeper seeing, and the possibility of a real body of work.
shootingBrief: Choose one narrow constraint. Shoot only inside it. Aim for 8–12 coherent frames. Write a one-sentence project statement. Volume 40–70.
technicalFocus: Settings: Keep approach and look consistent across the set.
Consistency of method strengthens the set more than variety.
Mix of candid and any approached portraits that fit the project.
failureModes: Project idea too broad to create coherence.
Inconsistent approach so the set does not hold together.
Abandoning the constraint when the street offers something else.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: Internal consistency of seeing, light, and approach. Strongest frames could continue as a real body of work.

title: Vertical / Horizontal
coreIdea: Make orientation an active decision rather than a camera default. Shoot half the session only vertical, half only horizontal, and compare.
whyItMatters: Default horizontal is lazy. Orientation changes emphasis, meaning, and relationships inside the frame.
shootingBrief: First half: only vertical. Second half: only horizontal. Revisit same scenes in both when possible. Minimum 6 strong frames in each orientation. Volume 50–80.
technicalFocus: Settings: Standard street settings for conditions.
Stance: Recompose fully for the new orientation. Do not simply rotate the camera.
Distance: Adjust as needed for the new frame shape.
failureModes: Simply rotating the camera without rethinking composition.
Weak verticals that are just cropped horizontals.
Defaulting back to horizontal when the exercise feels restrictive.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: Certain scenes clearly belong to one orientation, and you can articulate why.

title: Ethics
coreIdea: Shoot with a clear, personal, practical code. Make pictures you would be prepared to show the subjects or defend without rationalization.
whyItMatters: Technical skill without ethical clarity produces work that eventually feels extractive or hollow. This day forces the code into practice under real conditions.
shootingBrief: Normal street work with heightened awareness of consent, dignity, power, and potential harm. Avoid extractive situations. Minimum 6 frames you would show the subjects. Volume 40–60.
technicalFocus: No special settings. The constraint is behavioral and ethical.
Approached portraits: clear, brief, respectful communication.
Candid: continuous reading of the situation. Distance and stance should never feel predatory.
failureModes: Abstract principles that disappear when a strong picture appears.

goodVsExcellent.excellent: Pictures are strong and you have a clear personal rule set you actually follow under pressure.

reflectionPrompts: What is your personal rule for photographing strangers?
Have any previous keepers crossed a line in retrospect?
What kind of street photographer do you want to be?
closingNote: Build the habit of asking the right questions every time you raise the camera.
